blocker.summary: The causal chain for the sub_821D6C20 SIGSEGV is resolved down to a specific internal failure exit inside sub_821CC508 (r443/r444 pinpointed the exact -1-return site, right after a call to sub_821D4988 with a constant argument 0x8275a414). r445 decompiled sub_821D4988 (new tool, scripts/DecompileD4988Logger.java, committed) and found it is a generic 64-slot ring-buffer event/telemetry logger (lock, write, unlock, then a short wait treating WAIT_TIMEOUT as the normal outcome) -- not a diagnostic string printer, which explains why r444's attempt to read a string at that address came back empty: the argument is a raw numeric log payload, not a string pointer. More importantly, r445 live-tested and corrected the working hypothesis r443/r444 had been building toward (a failing file/content operation): breakpoints placed on the EXACT instructions of sub_821CC008's file-enumeration branch (path construction, file open -- r441 had shown this branch does real NtCreateFile-style I/O with a confirmed 'game:\%s' path format) never fire on this run. sub_821CC008 takes its OTHER branch (pure in-memory arithmetic, no file access at all) this time, so the file-enumeration hypothesis does not explain sub_821CC508's failure on this execution path. Named for r446: return to sub_821CC508's internals (already decompiled/disassembled) with file I/O ruled out, and live-trace the actual values compared right before the confirmed failure site (+6171) without presupposing a file-related cause. The native_vulkan_backend.cpp backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438) remains the other open, user-dependent thread.
